answer: A staked identity registry defeats Sybils by making each account a costly, unique physical commitment. Each agent locks a slashable bond and signs with a hardware key fused into one secure chip; to stay active it must quickly answer random sensor challenges, such as distinguishing a juniper from timber in a canyon image. A farmer cannot clone one good agent into a thousand accounts, because every fake needs its own chip and its own locked bond. Costs scale linearly with the number of identities, while a detected clone is slashed, so the attack destroys capital.
